questions.question: What is Flexbox in CSS? Explain the flex container and flex item properties.
questions.title: Flexbox Basics — Container & Item Properties Explained
questions.direct_answer:
What is Flexbox in CSS? Explain the flex container and flex item properties.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** display:flex, flex-direction, flex-wrap, justify-content, align-items, align-content; item properties: flex, flex-grow, flex-shrink, flex-basis, align-self, order.

**Classic weak answer:** Confusing justify-content (main axis) with align-items (cross axis); order depending on flex-direction.

**Senior finish:** Diagram main vs cross axis for row/column; show a responsive holy-grail layout with Flexbox.

interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Confusing justify-content (main axis) with align-items (cross axis); order depending on flex-direction
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Diagram main vs cross axis for row/column; show a responsive holy-grail layout with Flexbox

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Flexbox Basics — Container & Item Properties Explained** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What is Flexbox in CSS? Explain the flex container and flex item properties.

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **display:flex, flex-direction, flex-wrap, justify-content, align-items, align-content; item properties: flex, flex-grow, flex-shrink, flex-basis, align-self, order**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Confusing justify-content (main axis) with align-items (cross axis); order depending on flex-direction**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Diagram main vs cross axis for row/column; show a responsive holy-grail layout with Flexbox**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** display:flex, flex-direction, flex-wrap, justify-content, align-items, align-content; item properties: flex, flex-grow, flex-shrink, flex-basis, align-self, order
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **confusing justify-content (main axis) with align-items (cross axis); order depending on flex-direction** and what you do instead.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **display:flex, flex-direction, flex-wrap, justify-content, align-items, align-content; item properties: flex, flex-grow, flex-shrink, flex-basis, align-self, order** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Confusing justify-content (main axis) with align-items (cross axis); order depending on flex-direction** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

questions.question: What is the difference between justify-content, align-items, and align-content in Flexbox?
questions.title: justify-content vs align-items vs align-content — Flexbox Differences
questions.direct_answer:
What is the difference between justify-content, align-items, and align-content in Flexbox?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** justify-content: main axis; align-items: cross axis per line; align-content: distribution of multiple lines (only when flex-wrap:wrap).

**Classic weak answer:** Expecting align-content to do anything when flex-wrap:nowrap (default) — it only affects multi-line flex containers.

**Senior finish:** Show a visual 3-row example: single line (justify+align-items), multi-line wrap (align-content takes effect).

questions.question: What is the difference between flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis?
questions.title: flex-grow vs flex-shrink vs flex-basis — The flex Shorthand
questions.direct_answer:
What is the difference between flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** flex-basis is the initial size; flex-grow distributes extra positive space; flex-shrink distributes negative space; flex shorthand = grow shrink basis.

**Classic weak answer:** Using width alongside flex-basis and not knowing flex-basis wins when both are set (unless flex-basis is auto).

**Senior finish:** Show flex: 1 (= 1 1 0%) vs flex: auto (= 1 1 auto) vs flex: none (= 0 0 auto) and when to use each.
